people.name: Adham Bedir
people.title: CEO
owns: Adham owns the customers, the contracts, the prices, and every conversation with the client.
He sets the company direction, the monthly targets, and the final call on priorities.
He owns fundraising, the investors, and the company in the United States.
He owns the weekly update to the client and the month-end review.
people.whereWhen: He works remotely from the United States. He comes to Egypt for launches and big partnerships.
contactFor: Any problem that Moharam, Mano, or Ahmed Alaa cannot solve
Questions about the client
Strategy, new markets, and new customers
people.note: Moharam, Mano, and Ahmed Alaa contact Adham directly. Everyone else goes through their Portfolio Manager.

people.name: Youssif Siessa
people.title: CTO
owns: Youssif owns the technology: the dashboard, the tools, the integrations, and future AI products.
He owns quality. The QC team reports to him through Youssef Medhat.
He makes the technical decisions on the collection app, the exports, and data handling.
people.whereWhen: He works remotely from the United States. He talks to Youssef Medhat about quality every day.
contactFor: A bug in a tool or the dashboard, or a new feature request
How the collection app works
How the quality process is designed
people.escalateTo: Adham, for anything about customers, contracts, or prices.
people.note: He joins conversations with the client when the topic is technical.

people.name: Aly Siessa
people.title: CPO
owns: Aly owns what a worker wears on the head: rigs, mounts, caps, and phones, plus the next generation of collection hardware.
He owns hardware design in Egypt and hardware procurement in China.
He sets the hardware standards: camera angle, comfort, how long it lasts, and safety on site.
people.whereWhen: He works remotely from the United States. He reviews designs with Ali Ateem once a week.
contactFor: A fault in a rig or a mount that keeps coming back
A new kind of workplace that needs new hardware
Buying phones in large numbers
people.note: Ali Ateem does the everyday hardware fixes. The Planning and Logistics Lead handles orders and replacements in Egypt.

people.name: Moharam
people.title: Director of Operations
owns: Moharam owns field operations: every live site, every shift, and every daily target.
He manages the Portfolio Managers day to day: their books, their standards, and their launches.
He owns the operator bench: hiring through Mano, training, and which operator goes to which site.
He checks and approves every new site launch.
He is the escalation point for anything inside the operation: absences, incidents, phone shortages, footage waiting to upload, a repeat quality problem.
He does not deal with site owners or factory managers. The Commercial Director does.
He manages the Planning and Logistics Lead and works with the delivery partners every day.
people.whereWhen: He is in the field every day, moving between sites. He meets Adham and Mano daily.
contactFor: Any problem on site that a Portfolio Manager cannot solve
An absence, if the Portfolio Manager has not answered within 20 minutes
An injury or an incident. Tell him within 30 minutes.
A site below target, phones offline, or footage piling up and not uploaded
people.escalateTo: Adham, for planning, resources, partner problems, and any emergency, at any hour.
people.note: Full time from October 1. Moharam is responsible for everything that breaks in the field.

people.name: Mano
people.title: Chief of Staff
owns: Mano owns recruiting, training, the onboarding gate, compliance and safety, admin, and executive reporting.
The Head of People and Compliance reports to him, with the Trainers and the Compliance and Safety Manager under that seat.
He keeps the employee handbook and this map, and files the signed site agreement after the Commercial Director closes a site.
At 6:15 PM he gets the list of sites with no evening check-out and chases each one.
Payments are not his lane. Money questions go to the Finance Manager.
people.whereWhen: He is in Cairo, in the office and remote. He meets Adham and Moharam every day.
contactFor: Hiring, onboarding screening, and ID and consent forms
Wearer files, offer letters, and the handbook
Site contracts and site paperwork
A evening check-out that is missing
people.note: Everyone joins the company through Mano.

people.name: Ahmed Alaa
people.title: Finance Manager
owns: Ahmed Alaa owns payments, the books, cash, payroll, and the intercompany invoices to the parent company.
He pays sites, workers, staff, and partners on accepted hours, minus fraud flags, from our own audit.
He runs the weekly audit on Thursday with a checklist, and the month-end close.
He stores the signed consent forms and the ID photos, one folder per wearer.
He reports to Adham, not to the people who spend: the person who controls the money does not report to the person who spends it.
people.whereWhen: He is in Cairo. He makes payments once a month. He sends the invoice after the audit.
contactFor: Salary, payments, expense refunds, bonuses, and referral rewards
An invoice or a partner statement
Where a consent form or an ID photo goes
people.note: Payments above the approval threshold need a second approval from Adham.

people.name: Hiring now
people.title: Commercial Director
owns: This seat is the business closer: it owns the pipeline of sites and businesses.
It negotiates and signs site agreements under a scoped power of attorney. Adham approves the terms.
It is the senior external face of KMSC to site owners and factory managers. Moharam does not deal with them.
It walks every site before launch with Moharam and the Portfolio Manager, and closes every engagement.
The closer promises, the operator delivers: it sits beside Moharam, both reporting to Adham.
people.whereWhen: At the sites and with site owners, six days a week. Once hired.
contactFor: A new site, a deal, or a contract change
A site owner or manager who wants something
Payment or offboarding questions from a site or a partner

people.name: Mazen
people.title: Planning and Logistics Lead
owns: Mazen owns the phones, the hubs, the transport runs, the inventory, and the site kits.
He writes the dispatch schedule: which phones leave the store on which day, and to which site.
Any move of phones between places, or between parts of a site, needs his approval.
The Inventory Manager, the runners, and the hub attendants report to him.
people.whereWhen: The store, the hub, and the sites on the schedule. Part of the week remotely.
contactFor: The dispatch schedule and a site's start date
Gear, spares, and the kit
The hub, the internet line, the runners, and the hub attendants
Moving phones anywhere
people.note: He reports to Moharam in both views.

people.name: Hiring now
people.title: Inventory Manager
owns: This seat does the physical check-in and check-out of every phone and piece of gear at the store, against the registry.
It builds the kits from the dispatch schedule, keeps the labels and the shelf, and receives deliveries.
Nothing leaves the store without a signed row. Nothing comes back without one.
It holds the store 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM, and counts with the registry before the Thursday count.
people.whereWhen: At the store at the Central Cairo warehouse, 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM.
contactFor: Picking up or returning phones and gear
A kit that is short or a label that is wrong

people.name: Eyad
people.title: Portfolio Manager
owns: Eyad owns a portfolio of sites and a monthly hour target.
He runs the site operators. Mano hires them, Moharam assigns them.
He runs daily rotations, the 30-minute recording cycle, restarts, charging, and phone custody.
He answers each quality flag within 24 hours and corrects the worker that day.
He handles absences, no-shows, and first response to any floor problem.
The site lead submits the evening check-out form by 6:00 PM. He checks it.
He finds new sites for the portfolio. 10% referral on a signed site. The Commercial Director vets it, closes it, and does the paperwork with the law firm.
His book follows one hub area. Sites that cannot upload on their own line run to the hub.
people.whereWhen: He is on site every day, across his portfolio. He clocks in with the operators and clocks out once the gear is back and checked.
contactFor: First contact for every operator and wearer on his sites
Absence notices. Send them by 8:00 PM the night before.
Phone and gear problems
Anything an operator cannot solve
people.escalateTo: Moharam for anything on the floor: phones, straps, quality, people. The Commercial Director for anything with the site owner: payment, the contract, offboarding.

people.name: Hiring now
people.title: Portfolio Manager
owns: Each new Portfolio Manager takes a book of sites in one hub area.
The first two weeks are spent as an operator on the floor.
Moharam hires for these seats.
people.whereWhen: On site every day, across the book, once hired.
contactFor: Through Moharam, until the seats are filled

people.name: Site leads
people.title: One per floor with 20 or more phones. 130 at 500,000 hours
owns: The site lead does the 7:00 AM count with the Portfolio Manager.
The site lead runs the floor between the Portfolio Manager's visits. The operators on that floor, one for every ten phones, follow the site lead between visits.
The site lead sends the morning check-in by 9:00 AM and the evening check-out by 6:00 PM.
On a partner site, the partner's person for that site is the site lead.
people.whereWhen: On the floor for the whole shift, at one site.
contactFor: The floor, when the Portfolio Manager is not there
The evening check-out for that site
people.note: Pay step: a placeholder until the handbook sets it.

people.name: Operators
people.title: One per ten phones. 650 at 500,000 hours
owns: One operator per ten phones. They hand out phones, fit rigs, and check the camera angle. They run the 30-minute restarts, check at each reset, and watch storage and battery. At shift end they collect the phones and dock them.
They clock in and out every day and hand the gear to their Portfolio Manager.
people.whereWhen: On the floor for the whole shift, at their assigned site.
contactFor: Wearers with a phone problem talk to their operator first
people.note: Operators are KMSC staff. Wearers are the people who film: site employees or workers KMSC recruited. Both pass onboarding screening.

people.name: Youssef Medhat
people.title: Director of Quality Control
owns: Youssef Medhat owns quality control: every uploaded video is kept, flagged, or deleted the next day.
He owns the dashboard, the session reconciliation against the client's export, the wearer log, and the invoice schedule.
Flags reach the Portfolio Manager through his dashboard. A repeat problem goes to Moharam.
At scale the QC team leads and the Data Analyst report to him. Central planning belongs to Mazen.
people.whereWhen: He is in Cairo, every day. He sends flags out the same day.
contactFor: What counts as fraud
A flag you disagree with or want explained
The standards for angle, lighting, and framing
Questions about one recording session
people.note: Portfolio Managers answer every flag within 24 hours.

people.name: QC reviewers
people.title: One reviewer per 11,000 hours a month. 45 at 500,000 hours
owns: They review every video on the account. Team size depends on how many videos come in that month.
Mano hires the reviewers.
people.whereWhen: They work remotely, every day.
contactFor: Through Youssef Medhat

people.name: Ali Ateem
people.title: Hardware Design Engineer
owns: Ali Ateem designs the rigs and mounts and improves them step by step.
He finds the cause of repeat hardware failures and fixes it.
He designs new mounts for new kinds of workplaces.
people.whereWhen: He is in Cairo. He designs with Aly. He gets parts through the Planning and Logistics Lead.
contactFor: A rig problem that keeps happening across many phones
A site that needs a different mount

people.name: External
people.title: Sourcing agent, China
owns: An outside agent, not a hire. Buys phones and collection hardware in China in large numbers and manages the suppliers and delivery times.
Aly owns the relationship.
people.whereWhen: In China, after we hire someone.
contactFor: Through Aly, until the seat is filled

people.name: Hiring now
people.title: IT Manager
owns: This seat owns Hexnode and device management: enrolment, labels, location, lost mode, remote control, and settings on every phone.
It owns the upload hubs, the fiber lines, and network capacity, and keeps the device list matching the phone registry.
It reports to Youssif for standards, and works day to day in Cairo alongside Mazen.
Priority hire: needed at 25,000 hours.
people.whereWhen: Cairo, on the phone manager and at the sites when a phone needs hands on it.
contactFor: A phone that will not enrol, log in, or show a location
A missing phone: lost mode and wipe
A bug in a tool or a setting on the phones

people.name: Delivery partners
people.title: Partners outside the company
owns: Delivery partners are independent. They find their own sites, staff them, and deliver hours under their own agreement.
They follow every KMSC standard: onboarding screening, one account per person, and the quality rules.
people.whereWhen: At their own sites.
contactFor: Working together on operations, through Moharam
Payments, through Ahmed Alaa
people.escalateTo: Moharam, for operations. Ahmed Alaa, for money.
people.note: Partners are outside the org chart. Their people are not KMSC staff.

people.name: Hiring now
people.title: Head of People and Compliance
owns: This seat owns the people side end to end: recruiting, training, the onboarding gate, and the wearer files.
It owns compliance and safety: ID and consent audits, incident reports, data-protection procedures, insurance certificates, and site safety. Legal itself stays with outside counsel.
The Trainers and the Compliance and Safety Manager report to it at scale.
It reports the open seats, the days to fill, and the audit results to Mano every week.
people.whereWhen: The Cairo office and the sites. Once hired.
contactFor: An open seat, a candidate, or a first day
A consent or ID audit, an incident report, or site safety
Training for a new hire or a site with repeat flags

people.name: Planned
people.title: Trainers
owns: Two Trainers by November. They train every new operator, site lead, and Portfolio Manager before their first shift.
They run the pocket cards, the quizzes, and the refresher when a site's flags go up.
people.whereWhen: The sites and the office. Planned.
contactFor: Training for a new hire or a site with repeat flags

people.name: Planned
people.title: Compliance and Safety Manager
owns: ID and consent audits, incident reports, data-protection procedures, insurance certificates, and site safety.
Runs the checklists. Legal itself stays with outside counsel.
people.whereWhen: The office and the sites. Planned for November.
contactFor: A consent or ID audit
An incident report or an insurance certificate
Site safety

people.name: Planned
people.title: Area Operations Managers
owns: Two by November, four by December, by geography: West Cairo, East Cairo, the Delta, and the coast.
Each runs three to five Portfolio Managers. They sit between Moharam and the Portfolio Managers.
people.whereWhen: In the field, one area each. Planned.
contactFor: Anything a Portfolio Manager in the area cannot settle

people.name: Planned
people.title: Partner Operations Manager
owns: Owns the partner operator channel: Shedi, Mansoura, and partner operators in the Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Morocco.
Agreements, quarterly device audits, custody, and the weekly numbers from every partner.
people.whereWhen: The office and the partner sites. Planned for November.
contactFor: A partner's site, numbers, or phones
A partner problem before it reaches Moharam

people.name: Planned
people.title: Data Analyst
owns: Owns the daily number and the reconciliation that makes the invoices tie: sessions against the client's export, hours against the evening check-outs.
people.whereWhen: The office, on the dashboard. Planned for November.
contactFor: A number that does not tie

people.name: Planned
people.title: QC team leads. One per ten reviewers
owns: One team lead per ten reviewers. They hand out the lists, settle the videos nobody is sure about, and keep the calibration set.
people.whereWhen: Remote, with the reviewers. Planned for December.
contactFor: A reviewer's list or a disputed video

people.name: Planned
people.title: Runners. One per hub route
owns: One runner per hub route. They carry the phones to the hub every night and bring them back before 7:00 AM, signed for at both ends.
people.whereWhen: On the road, every night. Planned for November.
contactFor: A run that is late or a phone list that does not match

people.name: Planned
people.title: Hub attendants. One per hub per shift
owns: One attendant per hub per shift. They count, dock, upload, charge, log, and hand back every phone.
people.whereWhen: At the hub, overnight. Planned for November.
contactFor: A phone that did not finish uploading
